chunks: And ʿUqbah ibn Khālid narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Concerning a man who came to a mountain and split from it a channel whose water flowed for a year. Then another man came to that mountain and split from it another channel, and the channel of the latter carried away the water of the channel of the former.

He عليه السلام said: 'They are to be measured by the water-skins of the well, night by night, and it is to be examined which of them has harmed its counterpart. If the later one has harmed the first, then it should be blocked.'
And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم judged accordingly and said: 'If the first one took the water of the later one, then the owner of the later one has no claim against the first.'

key_terms.أَضَرَّتْ: caused harm or damage affecting the other's water right
key_terms.بِحَقَائِبِ الْبِئْرِ: by means of the well-buckets or water-skins used as a practical measure
key_terms.جَبَلًا: a mountain serving as the source from which the channels were opened
key_terms.سَبِيلٌ: a legal claim or grounds for action against the other party
key_terms.فَلْيَتَعَوَّرْ: it should be blocked or rendered unusable
key_terms.قَنَاةً: a water channel cut through land or rock to carry water
key_terms.يُقَايَسَانِ: they are to be measured or compared to determine the extent of impact

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one water channel diverts or harms the water flow of another?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on competing water channels drawn from the same mountain source. The harm caused by one channel to another is to be assessed through practical measurement, and judgment is based on prior right and actual damage. It also attributes this ruling to the judgment of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3420 - Narrated by Uqbah ibn Khalid from Abu Abdullah (as):
Regarding a man who dug a water channel from a mountain, and its water flowed for a year. Then another man came to the same mountain and dug another channel, but the second channel diverted the water of the first channel.
Imam (as) said: "They should measure the water flow using the buckets of the well, alternating night by night, to determine which channel has caused harm to the other. If the later channel has harmed the earlier one, then it should be removed."
And the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) judged similarly, saying:
"If the first channel has taken the water of the second channel, then the owner of the second channel has no claim over the first."
